title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs and schools
seoTitle: Paris cost of living and school protests

tea.why: Students and workers are demonstrating due to anger over rising living costs, soaring inflation, and poor conditions in public schools.
tea.want: Protesters are demanding better-funded schools, improved education resources, higher wages, and actions to address the cost of living.
tea.changed: Oct 28: The Paris prosecutor's office and interior ministry reported record numbers of arrests and extensive property damage following weekend clashes.

summary: Mass protests and rallies drew hundreds of thousands of participants across France, including Paris, to voice frustration over the rising cost of living, school funding, and public services. Organised in part by trade unions, student groups, and re-emergent yellow vest movements, the demonstrations began peacefully before turning tense near their endpoints. Authorities stated that masked individuals hurled projectiles, fireworks, and stones at law enforcement officers, who responded with tear gas, water cannons, and stun grenades. The nationwide unrest resulted in widespread property damage, shop closures, and extensive arrests across multiple cities including Marseille, Lyon, and Bordeaux. Government officials, including President Emmanuel Macron and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, condemned the violence and vowed a firm security response, while trade and retail chambers reported severe economic losses due to damaged storefronts and declining inner-city foot traffic.
response: According to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, authorities deployed heavy security forces, including up to 70,000 officers, and used tear gas, water cannons, and sound grenades to disperse crowds. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence and stated that those who caused destruction and looted municipalities would be prosecuted.

crowd.text: The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000

arrests.text: Nationally, according to authorities, arrests have exceeded 1,200

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Mass demonstrations and clashes occurred across France, with turnout estimated at over 400,000 by the interior ministry.
The French retail chamber reported severe economic losses and widespread property damage affecting thousands of stores.
Authorities reported record arrests exceeding 1,200 nationally, alongside a protester fatality and serious injuries.
